source.title: Questioning Representational Optimism in Deep Learning: The Fractured Entangled Representation Hypothesis
source.authors: Akarsh Kumar; Jeff Clune; Joel Lehman; Kenneth O. Stanley

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses neuron-level interpretability and reports qualitative findings about toy CPPN representations, but it does not test any of the listed claim versions: it gives no neuron-pole job-share audit or held-out explanation evaluation.
record.gate_note: The study's own CPPN comparisons and weight-sweep findings are recorded as related representation results, not as tests of the listed versions. Its GPT-3, GPT-4o, Othello, and other language-model examples are either illustrative or cited from other work, and do not report a neuron-pole audit or held-out neuron-explanation evaluation.
record.test_reason: A position paper with qualitative toy experiments on single-image CPPNs, comparing Picbreeder-evolved networks with SGD-trained ones. It reports no neuron-pole job shares and no held-out or simulation-based scoring of explanations. It runs no attribution graphs, no InceptionV1 analysis and no measured interpretable-neuron share across tools or architectures. Its LLM examples are anecdotal behaviour or cited work. Nothing in it bears directly on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors argue that conventional SGD can yield fractured, entangled representations despite matching outputs, while open-ended Picbreeder search yields near-unified factored ones. They present FER as a hypothesis with possible costs to generalization, creativity and learning, which merits further study. They also claim SGD shows FER in their experiments, including ReLU nets.
record.recipe_differences: The paper compares neuron-activation visualizations and weight perturbations in toy CPPNs; it does not use the neuron-pole auditing or held-out explanation-testing procedures in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported representation findings differ between Picbreeder-evolved and conventional SGD networks. The paper also reports that SGD-produced FER persists in the tested ReLU architectures; it does not quantify neuron-pole job shares.

fits_no_version.finding: For three toy CPPNs (skull, butterfly, apple), networks with identical architecture and output differ in neuron organization. Picbreeder-evolved networks have organized, reused, factored neurons; SGD-trained ones are fractured and entangled. Selected weight sweeps differ the same way.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In toy CPPNs with matched architecture and output, the training or search path, not capacity, determines whether individual neurons have clean, interpretable roles.

record.problems: The direct experiments use toy CPPNs generating single images, not modern language models. Representation judgments are qualitative, the displayed weight sweeps are selected examples, and the paper does not measure neuron-pole job shares or test explanations on held-out activations.

untested.parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or job shares.
No neuron-level shares for any language model, dense or MoE, at any scale. MoE is only speculated about (Section 6.4).
No analysis of the InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron. Superposition and polysemanticity are only asserted to be consequences of FER (Section 5.1), without data.
No measured share of interpretable neurons across tools, regularization or architectures. The CPPN contrast holds architecture fixed and varies the training path, and is qualitative.
No attribution graphs or circuit-sufficiency test.
No test of activating-example explanations against firing on held-out inputs.
No automated simulation scoring of neuron explanations.

missing.what: With ReLU-only architectures, the intermediate neurons of SGD CPPNs are still described as fractured and entangled (no rows).
missing.versions: none (related to the fits_no_version finding; loosely to V4's architecture claim)

missing.what: A PCA change of basis shows only slightly less fracture in the SGD skull. Basis-agnostic random-direction weight sweeps still separate Picbreeder from SGD (no rows).
missing.versions: none (related to the fits_no_version finding; loosely to V4's 'better tools' claim)

record.verdict_notes: I agree with the reader's T6/discusses classification and that every row links to none. The weight sweeps shown are hand-selected; the authors say they are 'broadly representative' and release all sweeps. The FER account of superposition could bear on V3 and V4 in spirit: it is the opposite of V3's 'misread' view and places the cause in the training path rather than architecture or tools. But it is argued, not measured at the neuron-share level.

versions.untested_parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or shares of one-job, two-job, and not-understood poles.
No neuron-pole job-share comparison across language models, dense or MoE models, or model sizes.
No analysis of the InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron or recursive generalization.
No estimate of interpretable-neuron shares in InceptionV1-sized vision models and no tool-quality or architecture sweep measuring such shares.
No attribution-graph test of whether a large model's own neurons suffice to explain behavior.
No test of whether explanations fitting activating examples predict where neurons fire on held-out activations.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: Picbreeder Skull CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Visualized neuron activations across the input space and described the internal representation.
rows.measure: Qualitative organization of intermediate neuron representations
rows.baseline: Conventional SGD Skull CPPN producing the same target image
rows.value: The representation is described as organized: symmetry appears early, and key features are represented once and reused across the skull.
rows.note: This is a qualitative toy-network representation finding, not a count of neuron poles with one main job.

rows.subject: Conventional SGD Skull CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Visualized neuron activations across the input space and described the internal representation.
rows.measure: Qualitative organization of intermediate neuron representations
rows.baseline: Picbreeder Skull CPPN producing the same target image
rows.value: The representation is described as a disorganized patchwork with many novel patterns; the two sides are not represented as symmetric until the output layer.
rows.note: The paper says this network matches the target output while its internal representation appears fractured.

rows.subject: Picbreeder Skull CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Swept selected individual weight values and observed changes to the output image.
rows.measure: Qualitative semantic coherence of output changes under weight sweeps
rows.baseline: Output at the unswept weight value
rows.value: The selected sweeps produce meaningful changes, including control of mouth opening, eye winking, eye width, and jaw width; the overall skull pattern is generally preserved.
rows.note: The authors state that sweeps were selected to show both methods in their best light while remaining broadly representative.

rows.subject: Conventional SGD Skull CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Swept selected individual weight values and observed changes to the output image.
rows.measure: Qualitative semantic coherence of output changes under weight sweeps
rows.baseline: Output at the unswept weight value
rows.value: The sweeps are described as producing meaningless distortions and usually breaking symmetry incoherently.
rows.note: The authors state that sweeps were selected to show both methods in their best light while remaining broadly representative.

rows.subject: Picbreeder butterfly CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Visualized neuron activations and described the internal representation.
rows.measure: Qualitative organization of intermediate neuron representations
rows.baseline: Conventional SGD butterfly CPPN producing the same target image
rows.value: The representation is described as organized, with y-axis symmetry emerging early and aspects of the output specified once.
rows.note: A qualitative toy-network result; it does not report neuron-pole job shares.

rows.subject: Conventional SGD butterfly CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Visualized neuron activations and described the internal representation.
rows.measure: Qualitative organization of intermediate neuron representations
rows.baseline: Picbreeder butterfly CPPN producing the same target image
rows.value: The representation is described as disorganized, with left and right wings encoded separately and high-frequency patterns stitched together.
rows.note: The target output is described as perfectly reconstructed despite the different internal representation.

rows.subject: Picbreeder butterfly CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Swept selected individual weight values and observed changes to the output image.
rows.measure: Qualitative semantic coherence and symmetry of output changes
rows.baseline: Output at the unswept weight value
rows.value: Sweeps are described as making human-recognizable changes while respecting y-axis symmetry.
rows.note: The paper supplies a database of all sweeps but characterizes the displayed sweeps qualitatively.

rows.subject: Conventional SGD butterfly CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Swept selected individual weight values and observed changes to the output image.
rows.measure: Qualitative semantic coherence and symmetry of output changes
rows.baseline: Output at the unswept weight value
rows.value: Sweeps are described as producing deleterious changes that frequently break symmetry.
rows.note: The paper supplies a database of all sweeps but characterizes the displayed sweeps qualitatively.

rows.subject: Picbreeder apple CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Visualized neuron activations and described the internal representation.
rows.baseline: Conventional SGD apple CPPN producing the same target image
rows.value: The representation is described as separating the background, apple body, and stem into distinct units that are later combined.
rows.note: A qualitative toy-network result; it does not report neuron-pole job shares.

rows.subject: Conventional SGD apple CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Visualized neuron activations and described the internal representation.
rows.baseline: Picbreeder apple CPPN producing the same target image
rows.value: The representation is described as fragmented and entangled, without a clear separation of apple, stem, and background.
rows.note: The authors describe nearly every neuron as being used in an entangled manner.

rows.subject: Picbreeder apple CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Swept selected individual weight values and observed changes to the output image.
rows.measure: Qualitative independence and semantic coherence of output changes
rows.baseline: Output at the unswept weight value
rows.value: Some weights are described as independently controlling features such as stem angle, apple size, and background; one weight swings the stem around the top of the apple.
rows.note: A qualitative account of selected weight sweeps.

rows.subject: Conventional SGD apple CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Swept selected individual weight values and observed changes to the output image.
rows.measure: Qualitative independence and semantic coherence of output changes
rows.baseline: Output at the unswept weight value
rows.value: Sweeps are described as entangling multiple concepts; changes to apple size also alter the stem, and stem color changes with the background.
rows.note: A qualitative account of selected weight sweeps.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
